title: Effect of zinc oxide nanoparticles and light-emitting diode radiation on the viability and differentiation of stem cell derived from human apical papilla.
first_affiliation: Department of Endodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, Dental Research Center, Hamadan University of Medical Sciences, Hamadan, Iran.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONPs) have shown potential in regenerative medicine, particularly when combined with light-emitting diode (LED) radiation. This study aimed to explore the effects of ZnONPs combined with LED radiation on human stem cells derived from the apical papilla (HSCAPs), focusing on primary outcomes of cell viability, odontoblast-like differentiation, and mineralization.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This in vitro experimental study utilized ZnONPs synthesized via a green method using pomegranate peel extract. HSCAPs were divided into four groups: control, ZnONPs-only, LED-only, and ZnONPs + LED (experimental group). Cell viability, a primary outcome, was assessed using the MTT (3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide) assay at 24 h. Odontogenic and osteogenic differentiation, evaluated through dentin sialophosphoprotein (DSPP), bone sialoprotein (BSP), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), and dentin matrix acidic phosphoprotein 1 (DMP1) gene expression using qRT-PCR, were assessed on day 7. Mineralization, determined through Alizarin Red S staining, was measured on day 14. The doses used were 1 μg/mL ZnONPs and 620-640 nm range, 85% total emission LED radiation at 5 mW/cm2 for 30 s, the energy density would be 6 Joules/cm2. Statistical analyses were performed using Kruskal-Wallis and dunn's post hoc tests. (P < 0.05).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Cell viability was highest at 1 μg/mL ZnONPs, comparable to control (p > 0.05), and decreased at higher concentrations (p < 0.05). Odontogenic and osteogenic gene expression, including DSPP, ALP, BSP and DMP1was significantly upregulated (p < 0.05) in the ZnONPs + LED group compared to all other groups. Alizarin Red S staining revealed the densest mineralization in the ZnONPs + LED group, followed by LED-only and ZnONPs-only groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The synergistic application of ZnONPs and LED irradiation significantly enhanced odontogenic and osteogenic differentiation and mineralization of HSCAPs, suggesting their potential utility in endodontic regenerative therapies.

title: Effects of photobiomodulation therapy on secondary healing of the palatal donor site after free gingival graft harvesting: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
first_affiliation: Department of Prosthodontics, University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Vietnam National University, Hanoi, Vietnam.

abstract.text: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated photobiomodulation (PBM) therapy for postoperative pain and secondary wound healing at the palatal donor site after connective tissue harvesting. Following PRISMA guidelines, five databases were searched through 20 October 2025 for randomized controlled trials comparing PBM therapy with appropriate controls. Primary outcomes were postoperative pain (visual analogue scale, VAS) and epithelialization; secondary outcomes were analgesic consumption, remaining wound area, and bleeding. Random-effects meta-analysis was used, risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Nine randomized controlled trials with 299 participants were included. Day-1 pain could not be pooled. No statistically significant difference in postoperative pain was observed at day 3 or day 7, with reductions of approximately 1.2 and 0.4 points on a 0-10 scale. Complete epithelialization at 14 days was more than twice as frequent, with no significant difference at day 21. The remaining wound area at day 7 was smaller by approximately 22 mm². Heterogeneity was moderate for pain and low for healing outcomes. PBM therapy may increase the proportion of palatal donor sites achieving complete epithelialization at 14 days. For postoperative pain the evidence is very uncertain, and no statistically significant reduction was observed at either pooled time point. Most trials carried a high or unclear risk of bias, and treatment protocols were heterogeneous. Larger trials with standardized dosimetry are needed to establish the clinical value of PBM therapy at the palatal donor site.

title: Effect of low-level laser therapy versus sham laser in reduction of orthodontically induced inflammatory root resorption in the adolescent patients undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment: A randomized controlled trial.
journal: Journal of the World federation of orthodontists
first_affiliation: Division of Orthodontics and Dentofacial Deformities, Centre for Dental Education and Research, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, India.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: This study evaluated the effect of low-level laser therapy (LLLT) on orthodontically induced inflammatory root resorption (OIIRR) during leveling and alignment and en-masse retraction in orthodontic patients. It also compared pain perception and treatment duration between LLLT and control groups.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This single-center, double-blinded randomized controlled trial enrolled 40 adolescent patients aged 13 to 24 years (LLLT: 17.2 ± 3.0 years; control: 18.4 ± 3.1 years), allocated 1:1 via block randomization. Group I received LLLT (980 nm diode laser; 100 mW; 8 J/cm2; 8 s/tooth) to maxillary incisors on days 0, 3, 7, 14, and monthly for 12 months; Group II received sham laser. OIIRR was assessed via root length on periapical radiographs at baseline (T0), 6 months (T1), and 12 months (T2). Pain was recorded using the Visual Analogue Scale during the first 7 days of leveling and alignment (P1) and en-masse retraction (P2). Repeated measures ANOVA with Bonferroni posthoc and unpaired t-tests were used for intra and intergroup comparisons.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Significant root resorption occurred from T0 to T2 in both groups. No intergroup differences occurred except at tooth 12 (T0-T1) and 21 (T0-T2), where LLLT patients showed greater resorption (P < 0.05). LLLT significantly reduced pain at P1 and P2 (P < 0.001), except on days 5 to 6 at P1. Leveling and alignment duration did not differ between groups (123.8 vs. 126.2 days; P = 0.487).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: LLLT did not reduce OIIRR or shorten leveling and alignment duration but significantly attenuated short-term pain, supporting its use as a nonpharmacological analgesic adjunct in orthodontics.

title: Acupoint-Propagated Sensation During Laser Acupuncture in Bell's Palsy.
first_affiliation: Department of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Beijing Tongren Hospital, Capital Medical University.

abstract.text: This study aims to report a distinct phenomenon of propagated meridian sensation elicited by non-invasive laser acupuncture in two patients with chronic Bell's palsy and to describe the associated clinical outcomes. Two patients with Bell's palsy were recruited from the outpatient department of Otorhinolaryngology at Beijing Tongren Hospital. Both patients received laser acupuncture three times per week using a Class IV laser device. Based on traditional acupuncture theory and clinical experience, a systematic approach was used to identify potential acupoints and laser parameters. Outcome measures included the House-Brackmann Facial Nerve Grading System, the Sunnybrook Facial Grading System, electromyography, electroneurography, and the blink reflex. Both patients showed clinical improvement following laser acupuncture treatment. This case report documents patient-reported sensations propagating along meridian pathways during laser acupuncture treatment for facial paralysis. Further studies are needed to investigate the relationship between these sensations and clinical outcomes and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

title: Three-dimensional alveolar ridge augmentation combined with photobiomodulation therapy for post-traumatic bone loss: clinical protocol, case report, and evidence review.
first_affiliation: Department of Periodontics, Bo.C., Islamic Azad University, Borujerd, Islamic Republic of Iran. derikvand1@iau.ac.ir.

abstract.text: Post-traumatic alveolar ridge deficiencies often involve three-dimensional bone loss, making dental implant placement highly challenging. Guided bone regeneration techniques, combined with fixation devices, soft tissue substitutes, and adjunctive photobiomodulation therapy, have been proposed to enhance predictability and clinical outcomes. A 46-year-old female with severe alveolar bone loss, insufficient keratinized tissue, and maxillary sinus pneumatization following trauma was treated. Simultaneous three-dimensional ridge augmentation was performed using cortical cancellous Regen Allograft stabilized with bone plates and tenting screws. An open sinus lift was carried out with graft placement beneath the elevated Schneiderian membrane and coverage with a collagen membrane. Soft tissue management included palatal tissue mobilization and placement of acellular dermal matrix (Regen Allograft) under the flap. Postoperative photobiomodulation therapy was applied using an 808 nm diode laser (0.2 W, 4 J/cm²) to enhance soft and hard tissue healing. After six months of healing, six implants (IRES, volution, SVB) were placed under guided surgery, followed by screw-retained prosthetic rehabilitation. Clinical and CBCT examinations were performed during a 24-month follow-up period. CBCT evaluation at six months demonstrated sufficient horizontal and vertical bone regeneration, enabling successful placement of six implants with satisfactory primary stability. Soft tissue healing progressed uneventfully, with favorable tissue maturation and minimal postoperative discomfort. Prosthetic rehabilitation was completed successfully, and clinical and radiographic follow-up over 24 months revealed stable peri-implant bone levels, healthy peri implant soft tissues, satisfactory esthetic and functional outcomes, and no biological or mechanical complications. This case demonstrates that combining bone grafting with fixation devices, sinus augmentation, acellular dermal matrix, and photobiomodulation can successfully manage complex post-traumatic ridge deficiencies. The multidisciplinary approach provided predictable functional and esthetic outcomes.

title: Biophotonics in the diagnosis and management of oral disease: A narrative review.
journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
first_affiliation: Department of Dentistry, Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul, Porto Alegre, Brazil. Electronic address: hiltch@gmail.com.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Conventional visual and radiographic examination reliably detects advanced lesions but lacks sensitivity (Se) for early ones, blinded by the complex oral environment. Biophotonic methods use light-tissue interactions to noninvasively reveal structural changes for improved clinical decision making. This review appraises biophotonic modalities spanning diagnostic and therapeutic applications in oral disease.

abstract.label: TYPES OF STUDIES REVIEWED
abstract.text: This narrative review, informed by an evidence hierarchy, prioritized Cochrane systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical guidelines, and consensus statements across caries, periodontal and peri-implant disease, oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMD), oral cancer, and endodontics. Clinical, in vivo, and in vitro studies were included when higher-level evidence was absent.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The evidence was mixed across disciplines. Quantitative light-induced fluorescence found high diagnostic accuracy in occlusal caries detection, with a 2025 meta-analysis reporting an Se of 0.86, specificity (Sp) of 0.82, and an area under the curve of 0.81 through 0.93 for incipient enamel lesions. A Cochrane review reported high Se but lower Sp for oral cancer and OPMD (Se 0.87, Sp 0.50). Photodynamic therapy achieved a pooled response rate of approximately 76% in oral leukoplakia and 60.6% across OPMD. The strongest clinical evidence supports photobiomodulation, with a guideline-level recommendation for the prevention of oral mucositis. Limited evidence precludes recommendations for periodontal and peri-implant disease, caries treatment, and endodontic applications.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS
abstract.text: Despite mechanistic promise, evidence supports only 3 biophotonic applications for clinical use: photobiomodulation for the prevention of oral mucositis, photodynamic therapy for oral leukoplakia, and fluorescence-based caries detection; other indications remain investigational. Clinicians should carefully interpret regulatory clearance and marketing claims when clinical evidence is absent.

title: Effect of photobiomodulation on recovery from oral soft tissue local anaesthesia in paediatric patients: a preliminary split-mouth randomized clinical trial.
first_affiliation: Vishnu dental college, Bhimavaram, Andhra pradesh, India, India. ziaulhaque.mohamed@vdc.edu.in.

abstract.text: Paediatric dental patients are particularly vulnerable to inadvertent soft-tissue injury following local anaesthesia (LA) This preliminary study evaluated. the clinical efficacy of 810-nm diode laser photobiomodulation (PBM) in reversing oral soft-tissue anaesthesia in paediatric patients. Thirty-four children aged 8-12 years requiring bilateral primary toothextractions under infiltration LA were enrolled in by consideration of ethical codes. Local anaesthesia was administered using 2% lidocaine with 1:80,000 epinephrine, as per the local infiltration anesthesia protocol. Participants were randomly allocated to receive both PBM and sham Laser with 7-10 days washout period between the two interventions. PBM was delivered using an 810-nm diode laser in continuous mode at 200 mW for 12 s per point at six predefined intraoral and extraoral sites. An independent examiner assessed soft-tissue sensation at 5-minute intervals by standardized bilateral palpation, using the non-anaesthetized side as the reference. The primary outcome was time to first assessment at which sensation on the anaesthetized side was judged normal. Data were analysed using a paired-samples t-test. Mean reflection time was significantly shorter in the PBM group (60.7 ± 27.3 min; p < 0.001) compared with the Sham lasergroup (78.2 ± 17.0 min). Subgroup analysis demonstrated significant reductions in reflection time in both maxillary and mandibular arches. Photobiomodulation using an 810-nm diode laser demonstrated a reduction in subjective soft tissue anaesthesia recovery time following infiltration LA in paediatric dental patients under the conditions tested.

title: Photobiomodulation Reduces Physiological Stress and Pain During Dental Diagnostic Procedures: The UM-DANE 1 Pediatric Clinical Trial.
first_affiliation: Clinical professor and chair, Department of Orthodontics and Pediatric Dentistry, University of Maryland School of Dentistry, Baltimore, MD, USA.

abstract.text: Purpose: To evaluate effectiveness of photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) in reducing physiological stress (as measured by heart rate [HR] change), self-reported pain, and anxiety during cold pulp testing and routine gingival probing in healthy school-aged children. Methods: This prospective, randomized, split-mouth clinical trial enrolled 30 children aged 7 to 12 years at the University of Maryland pediatric dental clinics from July 2025 to January 2026. Each participant received PBMT (multiwavelength LED device, Nuralyte™) on 1 primary molar and no treatment on the contralateral control tooth. Following a 2-minute waiting period, cold testing and gingival probing were performed. Primary outcomes were HR changes from baseline measured via pulse oximetry. Secondary outcomes included self-reported pain (Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale), anxiety (0 to 10 numeric rating scale), cold perception, cooperation level (Frankl scale), and duration of analgesia. Paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used for split-mouth comparisons. Results: PBMT significantly reduced HR changes during cold testing compared to control (2.23±8.95 versus 6.07±8.70 beats per minute [bpm]; mean difference=-3.83 bpm, 95% confidence interval=-6.89 to -0.77, P=0.016). For gingival probing, self-reported pain was significantly lower with PBMT (median within-subject difference -2.0 points, P=0.004). Sensory perception was preserved in both groups (93.3% positive cold response). Analgesic effects remained stable through 20 minutes post-application. No adverse events occurred. Conclusion: PBMT with a multi-wavelength near-infrared device reduced physiological stress and self-reported pain during pediatric dental diagnostic procedures while preserving sensory function, supporting its use as a promising nonpharmacological behavior guidance option.

title: Combined nanofibrous scaffold and photobiomodulation therapy for an incisor with internal root resorption and an open apex: a case report.

abstract.text: This case report describes a combined approach for managing internal root resorption (IRR) and an open apex using a nanofibrous scaffold and laser photobiomodulation (PBM). A 25-year-old man with a history of dental trauma presented with radiographic evidence of IRR and an open apex in a maxillary central incisor. The treatment protocol involved revascularization and placement of a nanofibrous scaffold at the apical third of the root canal system. Subsequently, a mineral trioxide aggregate plug was placed to provide a biocompatible hermetic seal, thereby preventing microbial infiltration and promoting the formation of a rigid tissue barrier. Laser-assisted canal disinfection was performed prior to scaffold placement to ensure the effective eradication of pathogens and create a sterile environment conducive to regeneration. Adjunctive PBM stimulated cellular metabolism, reduced inflammation, and accelerated tissue regeneration, further enhancing the healing response. Finally, the remaining defect was filled with a bioceramic sealer. The tooth was subsequently restored with a zirconia crown. A periapical radiograph obtained 24 months after endodontic therapy revealed optimal apical closure, resolution of the periapical lesion, and preservation of tooth function. This case highlights the potential of integrating advanced biomaterials and laser therapy in endodontic treatment, offering a promising solution for complex cases involving IRR and an open apex.

title: Flapless Piezoelectric Implant Surgery with Photobiomodulation: A Non-Clinical Mechanistic-Bayesian Framework and Study Protocol.
journal: Indian journal of dental research : official publication of Indian Society for Dental Research
first_affiliation: Department of Futuristic Dentistry, School of Dental Sciences, MRIIRS, Faridabad, Haryana, India.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Flapless guided placement, piezoelectric osteotomy, and photobiomodulation (PBM) each have individual biological rationale in implant surgery. Their combined, standardised use has not been prospectively validated.

abstract.label: AIM
abstract.text: The aim is to develop a non-clinical, mechanistic-Bayesian framework specifying the intervention, Bayesian prior distributions, and validation strategy for a future randomised trial comparing an integrated flapless piezoelectric PBM protocol against conventional guided flapped rotary placement.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: A selective, non-exhaustive narrative review, not a systematic review or formal evidence synthesis, was used to identify representative evidence. No predefined eligibility criteria, database search strategy, or PROSPERO registration was undertaken or is applicable to this article type. 48-hour pain (0-100 mm Visual Analogue Scale) and implant stability quotient (ISQ) at 3 months, both assessed by blinded evaluators.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The integrated protocol is biologically plausible but hypothesis generating. Prior distributions are derived from selective narrative evidence and carry acknowledged, formally quantified uncertainty, addressed through mandatory pre-specified sensitivity analyses. Pilot and definitive randomised trials are required before clinical adoption.

title: Photobiomodulation versus stabilization splint, both combined with self-management, for acute temporomandibular myalgia: 48-week outcomes of a partially randomized controlled study.
first_affiliation: Ha Noi Medical University, Hanoi, Vietnam.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Photobiomodulation (LLLT) is used for myogenous temporomandibular disorders (TMD), but longer-term comparative evidence versus stabilization splints alongside structured self-management remains limited. This study aims to compare pain reduction and maximum painless mouth opening after photobiomodulation+self-management (PBM + SM) versus stabilization splint+self-management (OS + SM), with an additional self-management-only comparator (SM), over 48 weeks.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This partially randomized controlled study enrolled 66 patients with DC/TMD-diagnosed acute masticatory muscle pain. Forty-four participants consenting to intervention were randomized 1:1 to PBM + SM (660-nm diode laser, twice weekly, 10 sessions) or OS + SM (maxillary stabilization splint worn at night, 8 h/day for 2 months). Both intervention groups received the same SM programme (education, habit modification, and jaw exercises for 2 months). A non-randomized convenience group received SM alone (n = 22). Assessments were performed at baseline and weeks 2, 4, 12, 24, and 48. Primary outcomes were VAS pain (0-10) and maximum painless mouth opening (MPMO, mm). Secondary outcomes included masticatory muscle tenderness and Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC). Longitudinal analyses used linear mixed-effects models.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: All groups improved over time, with earlier improvement in both intervention arms. In the randomized comparison, PBM + SM and OS + SM showed comparable week-48 outcomes for VAS pain and MPMO. No significant between-group difference in masticatory muscle tender points was observed at week 48 after Holm adjustment. Comparisons involving the SM-only group were exploratory.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Over 48 weeks, PBM + SM and OS + SM produced comparable improvements in pain and maximum painless mouth opening, with no significant between-group difference in masticatory muscle tender points at week 48.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06419738.

title: Clinical Effects of Photobiomodulation, Corticosteroids, and Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs Following Third Molar Surgery: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.
first_affiliation: University of Santa Maria Santa Maria Peru.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To systematically synthesize the effects and safety of corticosteroids, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), and photobiomodulation, as evaluated within the comparisons available in randomized clinical trials, for controlling postoperative sequelae after third molar surgery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251178943). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched without language or publication-date restrictions. Randomized clinical trials evaluating at least one eligible intervention and reporting pain, edema, trismus, rescue medication, or adverse events were included. Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane RoB 2, and a structured narrative synthesis was performed by intervention class, comparator type, outcome, and follow-up period.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Thirty-six randomized trials involving 1838 participants were included: 13 primarily evaluated corticosteroids, 11 NSAIDs, 7 photobiomodulation, and 5 direct or combined therapeutic comparisons. Twenty-seven trials were judged at low risk of bias, seven raised some concerns, and two were at high risk. Corticosteroids were frequently associated with reductions in edema and trismus within placebo-controlled and active-comparator trials; NSAIDs showed more consistent effects on pain than on edema or trismus; and photobiomodulation produced heterogeneous, protocol-dependent findings. Only a small number of trials directly compared different treatment classes. Substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis and a valid indirect ranking.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The three approaches may improve different postoperative outcomes, but the available evidence does not support a definitive hierarchy among them. Direct head-to-head trials with standardized outcomes, treatment protocols, and follow-up periods are required.

title: 630 nm light-emitting diode irradiation suppresses inflammation and promotes osteoblast differentiation in periodontal cell models - in vitro study.
first_affiliation: BioMedical Sciences Graduate Program (BMSGP), Chonnam National University, Hwasun, Jeollanam-do, Republic of Korea.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Periodontal disease involves persistent inflammation and alveolar bone loss. Photobiomodulation using light-emitting diodes (LEDs) may regulate inflammation and bone remodelling, but the optimal wavelength and irradiation timing remain unclear.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Human gingival fibroblasts and RAW 264.7 macrophages were irradiated with 525, 630, or 850 nm LED light before or after lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation. The effects of 630 nm irradiation were further evaluated in primary mouse calvarial osteoblasts, MC3T3-E1 cells, bone marrow-derived macrophages, and RAW 264.7 osteoclast precursors. Inflammatory mediators, nitric oxide production, cell viability, osteoblast differentiation, and osteoclast formation were assessed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among the wavelengths tested, 630 nm irradiation most consistently reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and secretion and decreased nitric oxide production without affecting cell viability. In primary osteoblasts and MC3T3-E1 cells, 630 nm irradiation at 5 and 10 J/cm² increased alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, osteogenic marker expression, RUNX2 protein levels, and Smad1/5/9 phosphorylation. In contrast, the same irradiation conditions did not significantly affect osteoclast differentiation or the expression of osteoclast-related markers.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Irradiation with 630 nm LED light suppressed inflammatory responses and promoted osteoblast differentiation without enhancing osteoclastogenesis. These findings suggest that 630 nm photobiomodulation may provide a balanced therapeutic approach for periodontal disease, although further validation in animal models and clinical studies is required.

title: Laser as an Adjunct in Endodontic Treatment in Dogs: Perspectives on a Conservative, Effective, and Safe Approach.
first_affiliation: Faculty of Veterinary Medicine and Animal Science, University of São Paulo, São Paulo, Brazil.

abstract.text: Crown fractures and subsequent pulp necrosis are common clinical findings in veterinary dental practice. While conventional endodontic therapy typically yields favorable outcomes, light therapies, such as antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) and photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT), have emerged as promising adjuncts for enhancing disinfection and tissue repair. However, standardized protocols for these therapies in veterinary dentistry remain scarce. This clinical case report describes the management of a maxillary incisor with pulp necrosis secondary to a coronal fracture in a dog. Following conventional chemomechanical preparation, aPDT was performed using 0.01% methylene blue as a photosensitizer and a 660 nm diode laser (100 mW, 9 J) delivered via an intracanal diffusing fiber. Immediately after the endodontic canal manipulation, the diode laser (PBMT; 808 nm, 3 J/point) was applied using contact transmucosal mode to modulate inflammation and stimulate periapical bone repair, followed by weekly sessions for 3 weeks. Radiographic and clinical follow-up at day 1, 2 and 8 weeks, and 1 year postoperatively demonstrated progressive alveolar healing and the absence of clinical symptoms. The combined use of aPDT and PBMT with the described laser parameters seemed to be a promising, conservative and effective approach to optimize root canal disinfection, promoting local analgesy and possible accelerating apical bone remodeling. The results suggest that light therapies are valuable tools for enhancing endodontic success in dogs.

title: Photobiomodulation therapy for the management of pain associated with temporomandibular disorders: a systematic review.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: To determine whether photobiomodulation (PBM; formerly low-level laser therapy) reduces temporomandibular disorder (TMD) pain relative to a concurrent comparator, to report the evidence by diagnostic stratum, and to appraise its certainty and dosimetric reporting.

abstract.label: STUDY SELECTION
abstract.text: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from January 2016 to July 2026 for controlled clinical trials of PBM for TMD-related pain in participants diagnosed by RDC/TMD or DC/TMD criteria. The review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered on the Open Science Framework (DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/YP8GW); screening, extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were duplicated independently.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Nine reports representing eight independent cohorts were included. Protocols were markedly heterogeneous in wavelength (635-940 nm), energy density (5-300 J/cm²), number of sessions, and follow-up, precluding quantitative synthesis. Pain decreased from baseline in most PBM groups, but placebo groups often improved comparably and between-group superiority was less consistent: three of five myogenous cohorts favored PBM and two did not. Only one trial prespecified myalgia and arthralgia as separate strata, favoring PBM for arthralgia but not myalgia. No trial reported the complete World Association for Laser Therapy (WALT) parameter set. Certainty was low for myogenous and very low for arthrogenous TMD.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Photobiomodulation demonstrates pain reduction superior to sham controls in several myogenous TMD trials. However, due to low GRADE certainty and evidence inconsistency, it should be considered a complementary treatment option rather than a standalone therapy.

abstract.label: CLINICAL RELEVANCE
abstract.text: TMD affects approximately 31% of adults and is a leading cause of chronic orofacial pain. PBM was safe, noninvasive, and free of reported adverse effects, and may be considered an adjunct within a conservative, multimodal plan for myogenous TMD. Clinicians should be aware that no preferred dosimetric protocol is established, that the joint-pain evidence rests on one small subgroup, and that placebo responses were substantial. PBM should not displace established conservative measures, and patients should be counseled that the expected benefit over placebo remains uncertain.

title: Photobiomodulation and the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in apexogenesis: Rationale and evidence gaps.
first_affiliation: Department of Orthodontics, School of Dentistry, Iran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran. Electronic address: bahramirashin@yahoo.com.

abstract.text: Apexogenesis is a vital pulp therapy that preserves vascularized pulp in immature teeth and relies on dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) and stem cells from the apical papilla (SCAPs) for continued root growth and apical closure. Wnt/β-catenin signaling has an established role in odontoblast differentiation, reparative dentinogenesis, and root development, although normal root development requires regulated rather than simply increased Wnt activity. Photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) is proposed to act through mitochondrial photoreception, and in vitro studies report increased expression of odontogenic/osteogenic markers and angiogenic factors (VEGF, TGF-β2) in DPSCs and SCAPs. Because these markers overlap with Wnt/β-catenin targets, a link between PBMT and this pathway has been hypothesized but not tested in these cells. This review addresses three questions: the role of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in root development and dentin repair; the mechanism that could link PBMT to this pathway; and the in vitro evidence for PBMT effects on DPSCs and SCAPs and its consistency. The evidence is heterogeneous and limited. Increased odontogenic/osteogenic differentiation was the most consistent finding. Reported effects on "proliferation" were inconsistent and were estimated mainly by MTT, a metabolic assay that does not measure cell division; no study used a clonogenic assay, and only one performed direct cell counts. No superior wavelength or fluence was identified. No study has examined PBMT-induced modulation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling in DPSCs or SCAPs, and the markers involved are not pathway-specific. Therapeutic benefit in apexogenesis therefore remains unproven; direct mechanistic studies, light-delivery studies through dentin, and animal models are priorities.

title: Photobiomodulation as a potential adjunct to improve the predictability of mandibular incisor autotransplantation to the maxillary lateral incisor site in orthodontic patients.
first_affiliation: Department of Orthodontics, School of Dentistry, Iran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran. Electronic address: bahramirashin@yahoo.com.

title: Clinical outcomes of surgical laser interventions and adjunctive photobiomodulation in osseous crown lengthening: A systematic review.
first_affiliation: School of Dentistry, Shiraz University of Medical Sciences, Shiraz, Islamic Republic of Iran. kiarashfereidouni@gmail.com.

abstract.text: To synthesize the available clinical evidence on laser-based interventions in osseous crown-lengthening procedures, considering surgical laser techniques and adjunctive photobiomodulation separately. A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science was conducted from database inception to June 2025. We included clinical studies involving adults undergoing osseous crown lengthening with laser-assisted surgery or postoperative photobiomodulation. Three reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts, assessed potentially eligible full-text articles, and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed at the outcome level using RoB 2 for randomized studies and ROBINS-I for the nonrandomized comparative study. Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, we evaluated findings using a structured narrative synthesis rather than meta-analysis. We included five clinical studies published between 2021 and 2024. Three evaluated lasers used during the surgical procedure, while two evaluated adjunctive photobiomodulation following conventional surgery. Some studies reported reduced intraoperative bleeding and improved surgical visibility with surgical laser techniques, although they did not consistently assess these outcomes using standardized quantitative measures. Periodontal and gingival-margin outcomes were generally comparable with conventional procedures. Findings regarding postoperative pain were inconsistent, with benefits reported in some but not all studies. Across two small studies using different irradiation protocols, adjunctive photobiomodulation was associated with reduced early postoperative pain at selected assessment times; only one study reported lower analgesic consumption. Among the four randomized studies, one assessed result was judged to have a high overall risk of bias and three raised some concerns; none was judged to have a low overall risk of bias. The nonrandomized comparative study was judged to have a serious risk of bias. Some studies descriptively reported potential intraoperative advantages with surgical laser techniques, while adjunctive photobiomodulation may reduce early postoperative pain at selected assessment times. Given the small and heterogeneous evidence base and its methodological limitations, current evidence remains insufficient to establish superiority over conventional osseous crown-lengthening surgery or to identify an optimal laser protocol.Clinical trial number: not applicable.

title: Caudal optogenetic spinal stimulation promotes better therapeutic outcomes than rostral optogenetic stimulation following a cervical spinal cord injury.
first_affiliation: Department of Rehabilitation Medicine, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, United States.

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Spinal stimulation, including optogenetic stimulation, is a promising therapeutic approach for promoting functional recovery after spinal cord injury (SCI). To date, most studies have delivered stimulation caudal to the level of the lesion. Therefore, there is a lack of understanding of how spinal stimulation rostral to the lesion may affect recovery. Here, we investigate the effects of optogenetic spinal stimulation rostral to the lesion site on forelimb functional recovery and axonal growth in a rat model of cervical SCI.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Female Long-Evans rats received a C4 hemicontusion, intraspinal injections of an optogenetic viral vector rostral to the injury site, and a micro-light-emitting diode (μLED) implant for optogenetic stimulation. Beginning 6 weeks post-injury, rats received 6 weeks of optogenetic or sham stimulation alongside forelimb reaching rehabilitation. Forelimb reaching success and growth-associated protein 43 (GAP43) percent area were compared with those in our previous study, which evaluated an identical paradigm, but with optogenetic stimulation positioned caudal to the injury.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The present results indicate that rostral stimulation did not enhance forelimb recovery on the forelimb reaching task and that forelimb reaching success was significantly higher in the caudal optogenetic stimulation group compared to the rostral stimulation group. Additionally, rostral stimulation did not enhance axonal growth within the cervical spinal cord compared with sham stimulation, whereas caudal optogenetic stimulation promoted significantly more axonal growth than rostral optogenetic stimulation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Overall, these results indicate that caudal optogenetic stimulation promotes a greater therapeutic impact than rostral optogenetic stimulation.

title: Comparative evaluation of hyaluronic acid spray and low-level laser therapy on wound healing following gingivectomy: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
first_affiliation: Akdeniz University, Antalya, Turkey. narzu@hotmail.com.

abstract.text: Gingivectomy wounds heal by secondary intention, prolonging recovery and postoperative discomfort; this randomized controlled trial compared low-level laser therapy and hyaluronic acid spray for early wound healing and postoperative pain after gingivectomy. Systemically healthy patients requiring gingivectomy were randomly allocated to receive either LLLT (940 nm diode laser, 3 W, 128.4 J/cm2, applied on days 0, 3, 5, and 7) or 0.04% high-molecular-weight HA spray (applied twice daily for 7 days). Wound epithelialization was quantified through Mira-2-Ton plaque-disclosing staining combined with digital planimetric analysis (ImageJ) at baseline and on postoperative days 3, 7, and 14. Secondary outcomes included gingival index (GI), full-mouth bleeding score (FMBS), probing pocket depth (PPD), and visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores. A total of 64 participants were enrolled and randomized (n = 32 per group). Both groups exhibited significant wound area reduction over time (p < 0.001). However, the HA spray group demonstrated significantly higher wound epithelialization percentages (percentage reduction from baseline in the non-epithelialized, disclosing-solution-stained wound surface area) than the LLLT group on days 3 (p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.39), 7 (p < 0.001; d = 1.12), and 14 (p = 0.044; d = 0.73). The HA spray group also reported significantly lower VAS pain scores on days 1 and 3 (p < 0.05). Periodontal parameters improved significantly from baseline to week 6 in both groups (all p < 0.001), with no significant between-group differences at week 6 for GI (p = 0.999), FMBS (p = 0.843), or PPD (p = 0.718). HA spray yielded significantly accelerated re-epithelialization and superior early pain reduction compared to LLLT following gingivectomy, suggesting it may serve as a practical, patient-friendly adjunctive alternative to laser biostimulation in postoperative wound management. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Number: NCT07034625.

title: Fluence-Dependent Effects of 940-nm Photobiomodulation on the Proliferation and Osteoblastic Differentiation of Human Periodontal Ligament Stem Cells.
first_affiliation: Clinic for Orthodontics, School of Dental Medicine, University of Belgrade, 11000 Belgrade, Serbia.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: Photobiomodulation (PBM) has been proposed to regulate periodontal tissue remodeling, but its effects on osteoblastogenesis in periodontal ligament stem cells (PDLSCs) remain highly dependent on laser parameters. This study investigated the fluence-dependent effects of 940 nm diode laser irradiation on the proliferation and osteoblastic differentiation of human PDLSCs. Methods: Six primary human PDLSC cultures were established and characterized using flow cytometry and multilineage differentiation assays. Cell proliferation was assessed after a single irradiation at fluences of 1, 2, 4, and 10 J/cm2. Osteoblastogenesis was induced using repeated irradiation regimens initiated at 2, 4, or 10 J/cm2 under suboptimal or complete osteogenic conditions and evaluated by Alizarin Red staining on day 21. The expression of osteogenic genes (RUNX2, BMP2, SPP1, TGFB1, COL1A1, ALPL, and BGLAP) was evaluated by qRT-PCR at different time points. Culture supernatants were analyzed for soluble osteogenic mediators. Results: The established PDLSC cultures had an MSC-like phenotype, robust osteogenic potential, moderate chondrogenic potential, and weak or no adipogenic potential. Proliferation of PDLSCs was considerably increased by PBM at 2 J/cm2 on day 7, whereas fluences of 4 and 10 J/cm2 inhibited proliferation. Osteoblastic mineralization was increased with the 2 J/cm2 irradiation regimen but was markedly reduced with the 10 J/cm2 regimen. Gene expression analysis confirmed this fluence-dependent response under optimal culture conditions. The 2 J/cm2 irradiation regimen significantly upregulated each analyzed osteogenic gene at one or more time points, whereas the 10 J/cm2 regimen downregulated RUNX2, BMP2, SPP1, COL1A1, and BGLAP. PBM at 2 J/cm2 also increased production of soluble BMP-2, OPG, PDGF-BB, ALP, and Leptin in a time-dependent manner. Conclusions: PBM exerts a fluence-dependent effect on human PDLSCs. A single irradiation at 2 J/cm2 increased proliferation, whereas the irradiation regimen initiated at 2 J/cm2 promoted osteoblastogenesis. In contrast, higher-fluence conditions, particularly the regimen initiated at 10 J/cm2, were inhibitory.

title: Comment on "Laser-induced modulation of root dentin surface for growth factor release and enhanced stem cell response".
first_affiliation: NEOSC, São José, Brazil. rodrigofariasodonto@gmail.com.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Laser conditioning of dentin has been investigated as a strategy to enhance growth factor release and cellular responses in regenerative endodontics. The recent study by Mokhtari et al. reported laser-induced modulation of root dentin, increased transforming growth factor-beta 1 (TGF-β1) release, and enhanced alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity. However, several methodological aspects should be considered when interpreting these findings and their potential clinical translation.

abstract.label: MAIN TEXT
abstract.text: A critical analysis identifies important limitations in the experimental design. First, all laser-treated specimens were previously exposed to sodium hypochlorite, without a laser-only control, preventing the independent determination of the effect attributable to laser irradiation. Second, the concomitant increase in TGF-β1 release and ALP activity demonstrates an association but does not establish a causal mechanistic relationship, as no inhibition or neutralization experiments targeting TGF-β1 signaling were performed. Third, the use of mature dentin obtained from adult teeth limits direct extrapolation to immature permanent teeth, which are the clinical context emphasized in regenerative endodontics. In addition, the use of stem cells from human exfoliated deciduous teeth (SHED) does not fully represent endogenous cell populations involved in regenerative endodontics, and cellular migration or chemotaxis was not evaluated. Finally, differences in power and exposure time among wavelengths, together with the absence of calibrated power measurements and direct temperature monitoring, limit interpretation of dosimetry, dose-response relationships, and thermal safety.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: The findings provide preliminary evidence that laser irradiation may modify dentin and influence growth factor release and cellular responses. Nevertheless, laser-only controls, mechanistic assessment of TGF-β1 signaling, immature dentin models, evaluation of cellular migration, calibrated laser dosimetry, and temperature monitoring are necessary to strengthen the mechanistic and translational evidence supporting laser-assisted regenerative endodontic applications.

title: Umbrella review of low-level light therapy: evidence across clinical conditions.
first_affiliation: Global Cooperation Center, Korea Institute of Oriental Medicine, Daejeon, Korea, Republic of.

abstract.text: Low-level light therapy (LLLT) and photobiomodulation (PBM) have been studied in diverse clinical fields. Although numerous systematic reviews have been published, their findings are fragmented and inconsistent. This umbrella review of systematic reviews aimed to synthesize the evidence on the effectiveness and safety of LLLT across various clinical conditions. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science databases were searched from inception to February 24, 2026. Eligible studies were systematic reviews or meta-analyses of LLLT in humans. Data on clinical conditions, intervention characteristics, overall direction of conclusions, and adverse events were extracted. Methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2. A total of 100 systematic reviews were included, representing 1,164 primary-study occurrences and 790 unique eligible primary studies. Oral and dental conditions accounted for the largest evidence base (53 reviews), followed by musculoskeletal disorders (22 reviews), oncology-related complications (8 reviews), and wound and lymphatic conditions (8 reviews). Overall, 62 reviews reached conclusions favoring the evaluated intervention, 34 reported neutral or mixed conclusions, and 4 had unclear conclusions. The highest proportion of favorable conclusions was observed for oncology-related complications. Of the 100 reviews, 11 reported one or more adverse events or side effects, 32 explicitly reported no adverse events, and 57 did not provide adverse-event information. Most reviews received low (30.0%) or critically low (60.0%) overall confidence ratings using AMSTAR 2. The review literature suggests potential clinical benefit of LLLT in selected indications, particularly oncology-related complications such as oral mucositis. However, these descriptive patterns do not establish treatment efficacy or the certainty of the underlying evidence. Heterogeneity in treatment parameters, generally low methodological confidence, and incomplete adverse-event reporting limit interpretation and preclude firm conclusions about safety.

title: Photobiomodulation-Mediated Modulation of TGF-β/Smad Signaling in Stem Cell-Driven Osteogenesis.
first_affiliation: Laser Research Centre, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Johannesburg, Doornfontein, South Africa.

abstract.text: Bone regeneration remains a significant clinical challenge as a result of limitations presented by autografts, allografts, and synthetic implants. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) serve as key drivers of osteogenesis as they can differentiate into osteoblasts and osteocytes. This process is, however, regulated by the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling pathway, which can upregulate the Runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) to promote early proliferation and commitment through canonical Smad signaling, and also inhibit late-stage differentiation to prevent excessive matrix deposition. These responses are refined further by noncanonical pathways. Photobiomodulation (PBM), a noninvasive light-based therapy, has emerged as a promising modulator of stem cell-driven osteogenesis, as it can interact with the TGF-β/Smad pathway. PBM exerts effects on the mitochondria, activating cytochrome c oxidase, increasing ATP production, and generating reactive oxygen species in a controlled manner. This leads to a stimulation of MSC proliferation, migration, and osteogenic differentiation. Emerging evidence from various studies shows that PBM can also modulate TGF-β/Smad signaling by activating latent TGF-β, enhancing Smad phosphorylation, and modulating the noncanonical pathways. However, evidence examining this interaction specifically during MSC osteogenesis are few, and the mechanisms underlying their interaction are incompletely understood. This review, therefore, critically examines existing evidence to elucidate some of these mechanisms for MSC osteogenesis. Although it is promising, challenges still exist in standardizing PBM parameters and conducting targeted studies in clinically relevant three-dimensional models. A clearer understanding of these interactions could provide a basis for future research aimed at advancing noninvasive regenerative strategies for bone defects and osteoporosis.

title: Photobiomodulation therapy and Wnt/β-catenin signaling in periodontal ligament stem cells during orthodontic tooth movement: A hypothesis and literature review.
first_affiliation: Department of Orthodontics, School of Dentistry, Iran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran. Electronic address: bahramirashin@yahoo.com.

abstract.text: Orthodontic treatment usually takes 18 to 36 months that can lead to time-dependent side effects (like caries and root resorption). Hence, there is growing interest in safely accelerating orthodontic tooth movement (OTM). Photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) has been proposed as a non-invasive approach to accelerate OTM, but clinical findings are inconsistent. Discrepancies may be due to irradiation protocols (light source, wavelength, energy density, exposure time), the orthodontic stage at which PBMT is applied, and the appliance used. A common component across these settings is the periodontal ligament stem cell (PDLSC). PDLSCs are mechanosensitive progenitor cells that contribute to the stress-strain response underlying OTM, and canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling is a key, but not the sole, regulator that balances OPG- and RANKL-mediated bone resorption against osteogenic bone formation; inflammatory mediators, non-coding RNAs, epigenetic mechanisms, and patient-related factors also regulate periodontal remodeling. In vitro studies indicate that PBMT affects PDLSC proliferation, osteogenic differentiation, and RANKL/OPG expression; only one preliminary study, in unloaded cells and at transcript level, suggests that it may upregulate Wnt/β-catenin and TGF-β pathway components. On this basis, we propose a hypothetical framework in which PBMT-related mitochondrial and redox signaling might intersect with force-induced Wnt activation, with each link graded by level of evidence. This framework is unconfirmed: no study has combined orthodontic-like loading, characterized PDLSCs, and multi-level assessment of Wnt/β-catenin signaling under PBMT, and faster movement should not be assumed advantageous without periodontal safety data. Mechanistic and in vivo studies, including inhibition experiments, are needed.

title: A Low-Cost Portable Machine Vision System for Non-Destructive Density Estimation of Dunaliella sp. Cultures.
first_affiliation: College of Information Engineering, Dalian Ocean University, Dalian 116023, China.

abstract.text: Routine microalgal cell counting requires sampling and microscopy. We developed a low-cost portable machine-vision system (LPMVS) for non-destructive density estimation of visibly green Dunaliella sp. cultures. The compact benchtop LPMVS combines motorized flask loading, a light-isolated dark box with diffuse light-emitting diode (LED) illumination, fixed camera-flask geometry, red-green-blue (RGB) imaging through the flask, mask-derived liquid-region extraction, Raspberry Pi inference, and a local liquid-crystal display (LCD). A ready-state load-to-unload cycle required approximately 37 s, including 6 s of processing. The two 40-day flask trajectories yielded 240 image-hemocytometer pairs; 200 records were used to compare three regressors with 20 features selected from 339 descriptors. K-nearest neighbors (KNN) performed best in the flask-mixed record-level comparison (R2 = 0.98; mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) = 6.41%; n=40). Reciprocal leave-one-flask-out transfer analysis on complete trajectories with independently retrained pipelines gave KNN R2 values of 0.914 and 0.803. In the reverse direction, R2 was 0.936 within the overlapping range (n=79), but 41 above-range densities were systematically underestimated. Bootstrap resampling identified recurrent color-based features in both trajectories. An edge-device check using 10 additional measurements yielded preliminary reference-density tracking (R2 = 0.94). These findings support the feasibility of the LPMVS workflow for non-destructive monitoring under controlled laboratory conditions, but extrapolation and generalization to independent batches and optical configurations remain unestablished.

title: Low-level light therapy for dry eye disease and meibomian gland dysfunction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
first_affiliation: Department of Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, Oslo University Hospital, Oslo, Norway.

abstract.text: A healthy tear film is vital for ocular surface integrity and relies on the coordinated function of the lacrimal glands, meibomian glands and conjunctival goblet cells. Dysfunction in any of these elements can lead to dry eye disease (DED). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy of low-level light therapy (LLLT) as a standalone DED treatment. Although evidence for LLLT's therapeutic potential is growing, prior reviews have focused on short-term outcomes or combined LLLT with intense pulsed light. This meta-analysis consolidates current findings to clarify the clinical value of LLLT monotherapy in DED management. We systematically searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials for studies evaluating LLLT for DED. Study selection and data extraction were conducted according to pre-specified inclusion and exclusion criteria. Meta-analyses were performed for Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), non-invasive break-up time (NIBUT) and tear meniscus height (TMH). Ten clinical studies were eligible for our systematic review, which included a total of 473 participants. Irradiation protocols included treatment sessions using wavelengths of 625-640 nm and/or 810-850 nm, with each session lasting a minimum of 10 min. In our meta-analyses, LLLT monotherapy was associated with significant improvements in OSDI (weighted mean difference [WMD] -11.42, p < 0.00001), NIBUT (WMD +1.49 s, p = 0.005), and TMH (WMD +0.04 mm, p = 0.007). Sensitivity analyses restricted to eligible RCTs confirmed significant effects on OSDI and NIBUT, but not on TMH. No adverse events were reported. LLLT appears to be well tolerated and may improve signs and symptoms of DED, particularly ocular discomfort. It may represent a promising standalone treatment option for patients in whom combination regimens involving IPL treatment are contraindicated.

title: The oral microbiome in the biological and clinical response to photobiomodulation during cancer supportive care: a critical mechanistic and translational review.
first_affiliation: Department of Orthodontics, Dental School, Iran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran. Electronic address: Dr.shahriar.eftekharian92@gmail.com.

abstract.text: Cancer therapy can disrupt the oral microbial ecosystem through mucosal injury, salivary dysfunction, immune suppression, antimicrobial exposure, dietary change, and altered oral hygiene. Photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) is guideline-supported for prevention of oral mucositis in selected oncologic settings, but whether the oral microbiome contributes to PBMT response remains uncertain. This critical narrative review reframes the question from whether PBMT changes the oral microbiome to what role, if any, microbial ecology plays in the biological and clinical response to PBMT during cancer supportive care. Evidence is organized as direct clinical evidence, indirect clinical evidence, experimental microbial evidence, and mechanistic hypothesis. Direct clinical evidence is sparse and internally mixed: a four-patient uncontrolled pilot reported concurrent cytokine and microbiome shifts after PBMT, whereas a 2023 head-and-neck cancer case series reported clinical improvement in mucositis without significant pre-post changes in salivary bacterial community structure. The strongest current rationale therefore supports a host-first model in which PBMT modifies epithelial integrity, inflammatory and redox signaling, tissue repair, and possibly salivary physiology, thereby changing the ecological conditions experienced by oral microorganisms. Direct microbial photobiological effects remain plausible but are highly dependent on wavelength, irradiance, radiant exposure, oxygen availability, organism, and biofilm state, and should not be conflated with antimicrobial photodynamic therapy. We propose four non-equivalent roles for microbiome change: mediator, modifier, biomarker, or consequence of treatment response. Oral mucositis is the most informative clinical model, but causal interpretation requires longitudinal sampling, functional microbial assays, complete PBMT dosimetry, validated clinical and patient-reported outcomes, and rigorous control of antimicrobials, periodontal status, oral hygiene, diet, feeding support, and anticancer treatment. Microbiome modulation should currently be regarded as an emerging mechanistic hypothesis and research endpoint rather than an established mechanism of PBMT efficacy.

title: Treatment of Oral Mucosa Self-Injury in Older Patient With Neurological Disorder: Case Report.
first_affiliation: Geriatric Dentistry Discipline, University of Western São Paulo - Presidente Prudente, São Paulo, Brazil.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To describe the management of oral self-injury in an older patient with neurological impairment using a digitally fabricated mouthguard.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Oral self-injury may be challenging in patients with neurological conditions.

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: An acrylic resin mouthguard was fabricated from intraoral scans for an 82-year-old bedridden woman. Photobiomodulation and oral hygiene measures were also used.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The lesion healed, and recurrent trauma was prevented.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Intraoral scanning enabled comfortable fabrication of the oral device.

title: Effect of Low-Level Laser Therapy on Stability of Dental Implants in D3 and D4 Bone Quality: A Split-Mouth Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
journal: The International journal of oral & maxillofacial implants

abstract.label: PURPOSE
abstract.text: Achieving predictable implant stability in low-density maxillary bone (D3-D4) remains clinically challenging because reduced bone density is associated with greater early loss of stability and an increased risk of implant failure. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has been proposed to enhance osseointegration; however, clinical evidence regarding its effect on implant stability in low-density bone remains limited and inconsistent. The aim of this study is to evaluate the effect of 940-nm diode laser photobiomodulation (PBM) on implant stability during early healing in low-density maxillary bone (D3-D4).

abstract.label: MATERIALS AND METHODS
abstract.text: This split-mouth, randomized controlled clinical trial included medically healthy adults who required bilateral maxillary implants. A total of 40 implants were placed in 10 participants using a guided flapless protocol. Test sites received 940-nm diode laser PBM immediately after implant placement and at 2-week intervals for 2 months, while contralateral sites served as controls. Implant stability was measured using resonance frequency analysis and expressed as implant stability quotient (ISQ) at baseline (T0), 2 months (T1), and 3 months (T2). Data was analyzed using linear mixed-effects model as primary analysis and two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance as supportive.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In the primary mixed-effects analysis, implant stability did not differ significantly between the PBM and control groups at baseline (estimated mean difference [PBM control], -2.45 ISQ; P = 0.341). At 2 months, PBM-treated implants demonstrated significantly higher estimated stability than control implants (mean difference, 6.30 ISQ; 95% CI, 1.21-11.39; P = 0.016). At 3 months, no significant between-group difference was observed (mean difference, 0.40 ISQ; P = 0.878). The linear mixed-effects model demonstrated a significant time × treatment interaction (P = 0.042), indicating that implant-stability trajectories differed between the groups over time. The complete-case repeated-measures ANOVA yielded a consistent significant time × treatment interaction (P = 0.007). No adverse effects related to PBM were observed.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Photobiomodulation using a 940-nm diode laser enhanced early implant stability and reduced the magnitude of the stability dip in D3-D4 maxillary bone without affecting final implant stability after 3 months. PBM may represent a safe adjunctive approach to support early osseointegration in low-density bone.

title: 940-nm Photobiomodulation Enhances ADSC-Mediated Tracheal Cartilage Repair through TRPV1-Associated Calcium Signaling and Mitochondrial Redox Remodeling.
first_affiliation: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital, Tongji University School of Medicine, Shanghai 200443, China.

abstract.text: Tracheal cartilage repair requires simultaneous restoration of a stable cartilage matrix, airway patency, and mechanical support, yet the regenerative state of implanted stem cells remains difficult to control. Here, we show that 940-nm photobiomodulation (PBM) enhances the chondrogenic competence of adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) within a defined dose window. Among the radiant exposures tested, 50 J/cm2 most effectively promoted cell-cycle progression, cartilage-matrix formation and expression of SRY-box transcription factor 9, type II collagen, and aggrecan, while suppressing fibrotic, hypertrophic, and catabolic markers. These effects were not reproduced by a temperature-matched heat control. In 3-dimensional porous scaffolds, preconditioned ADSCs exhibited improved survival, spreading, matrix deposition, and mechanical performance. Mechanistically, 940-nm PBM remodeled mitochondrial architecture, membrane potential, respiration, cellular adenosine triphosphate content and redox status. Pathway perturbation implicated transient receptor potential vanilloid 1-associated Ca2+ signaling, a redox-dependent component of Akt/glycogen synthase kinase 3β activation and SRY-box transcription factor 9 nuclear localization in the chondrogenic response. Preconditioning also preserved cartilage-associated gene expression under inflammatory challenge and altered macrophage-associated inflammatory marker profiles. In a rabbit tracheal cartilage defect model, constructs preconditioned at 50 J/cm2 improved cartilage-like tissue formation, epithelial repopulation, lumen patency, and mechanical function. These findings support repeated 940-nm PBM conditioning as a controllable ex vivo strategy for enhancing ADSC chondrogenic competence and improving early tracheal cartilage repair across cellular and tissue scales.

title: 660 nm LED preconditioning programs mitochondrial signaling in BMSCs for functional tracheal cartilage regeneration.
first_affiliation: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital, Tongji University School of Medicine, Shanghai, China.

abstract.text: Stem-cell-based cartilage regeneration is limited not only by cell delivery, but also by the difficulty of establishing a stable and functionally competent regenerative cell state before implantation. Here, we report a photonic mitochondrial programming strategy in which 660 nm light-emitting diode (LED) irradiation preconditions bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) to enhance functional tracheal cartilage regeneration. BMSCs were seeded onto egg white-derived ring-shaped porous scaffolds and exposed to defined 660 nm LED irradiation before implantation. Among the tested irradiation conditions, 15 J/cm2 optimally promoted BMSC proliferation, chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage-like extracellular matrix deposition, while suppressing fibrotic, hypertrophic and matrix-degrading phenotypes. Mechanistically, 660 nm LED irradiation enhanced cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) activity, mitochondrial membrane potential, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production and respiratory function, accompanied by moderate reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling. This mitochondrial bioenergetic-redox response activated the PI3K/Akt/mTOR/GSK3β-SOX9 axis, thereby promoting type II collagen, aggrecan and glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix formation. Pharmacological inhibition of ROS signaling, mitochondrial activity, PI3K or mTOR attenuated the LED-induced chondrogenic program. In a rabbit tracheal cartilage ring defect model, 15 J/cm2-preconditioned BMSC-scaffold constructs improved cartilage-like tissue formation, airway epithelial repair, lumen patency and mechanical support after 30 days of observation. These findings support 660 nm LED irradiation as a controllable mitochondrial preconditioning strategy for stem-cell-based functional cartilage regeneration.

title: Er:YAG Laser-Assisted Versus Conventional Surgery for Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal of Randomised Evidence.
first_affiliation: General Surgery, Homerton University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, London, GBR.

abstract.text: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a serious complication of antiresorptive and antiangiogenic therapy. Er:YAG (erbium-doped yttrium aluminium garnet) laser-assisted surgery has been proposed as an adjunct to conventional debridement, but randomised evidence is limited. This PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420261509183), conducted according to PRISMA 2020, searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library through September 10, 2026 for randomised studies comparing laser-assisted surgery with conventional surgical treatment of MRONJ. Thirteen full-text articles were assessed, and one randomised controlled trial met eligibility criteria. The trial report contains inconsistent participant accounting; its methods and results state that 72 patients were randomised and 65 completed follow-up, whereas the abstract and trial registry report 65 participants. No meta-analysis was performed. In complete-case analyses over 24 weeks of follow-up, adjunctive Er:YAG laser surgery was associated with higher short-term complete mucosal healing (85.7% vs 26.7%; review-calculated risk ratio (RR) 3.21, 95% CI 1.75-5.91), fewer postoperative complications (17.1% vs 60.0%; RR 0.29, 95% CI 0.13-0.63), and lower pain scores at three and six months, with longer procedure duration. Extreme-case sensitivity analyses for seven patients without reported healing outcomes did not change the direction of effect. Risk of bias raised some concerns for all outcomes. GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) certainty was low for healing, complications, and pain, very low for necrosis, and moderate for procedure duration. These apparent benefits derive from a single small trial, with low to very low certainty for all clinical outcomes, and apply only to adjunctive Er:YAG ablation in stage II-III MRONJ. They should not be extrapolated to photobiomodulation, other laser modalities, or other disease stages. Independent randomised evidence is required before its effectiveness can be established.

title: Emerging therapeutic strategies for medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw: From microenvironmental modulation to precision medicine (Review).
first_affiliation: Department of Stomatology, The Sixth Affiliated Hospital of Jinan University, Jinan University, Dongguan, Guangdong 523000, P.R. China.

abstract.text: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a challenging complication associated primarily with antiresorptive and antiangiogenic therapies. Its pathogenesis involves a complex interplay of impaired bone remodeling, angiogenesis, inflammation and infection, immune regulation and soft tissue healing. Established management includes conservative care, antimicrobial and symptomatic treatment when indicated and surgical intervention, however clinical outcomes remain variable. The present review aimed to summarize pharmacological, regenerative, biomaterial-based and physical or adjunctive strategies targeting the pathological microenvironment of MRONJ, with emphasis on their mechanisms of action and clinical evidence. The present review also examines the potential role of precision medicine in individualized risk assessment and treatment. Teriparatide, pentoxifylline/tocopherol, autologous platelet concentrates and human amniotic membrane have varying degrees of clinical support, although evidence remains limited or heterogeneous for several approaches. By contrast, geranylgeraniol, hydrogels, most mesenchymal stromal cell-based or cell-derived strategies, natural products and melatonin are supported predominantly by preclinical or limited clinical evidence. Other adjunctive approaches, including hyperbaric oxygen, ozone therapy, photobiomodulation, laser-assisted surgery and antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, require further validation. Overall, these strategies may complement established management, but their clinical readiness varies. Standardized clinical studies and integration of multidimensional patient data may facilitate more robust evaluation and individualized MRONJ management.

title: Comparison of the effects of different dental pulp stem cell preconditioning protocols on the odontogenic potential of their derived small extracellular vesicles.
first_affiliation: Oral Biology Department, Faculty of Dentistry, Mansoura University, Mansoura, Egypt. Dr_rana_nagah@mans.edu.eg.

abstract.text: Regenerative endodontic therapy that is based on the use of stem cells or their derivatives to induce dentin-pulp complex regeneration has recently gained substantial interest. This study aimed to compare the effect of preconditioning through odontogenesis (OD) and/or low-level laser therapy photobiostimulation (LLLT) of human dental pulp stem cells (hDPSCs) on the regenerative potentials of their derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) aiming to develop a novel pulp capping therapy. In the current study, hDPSCs were subjected to OD, LLLT, or dual preconditioning protocols before the isolation of sEVs, then the derived sEVs were co-cultured with naïve hDPSCs. Cell viability and wound healing capacity were evaluated using MTT and scratch assays, respectively. RT-qPCR was performed for odontogenic gene expression (DSPP, DMP1, and COL1A1), followed by immunocytochemical staining. Matrix mineralization was also assessed, and relevant statistical analyses were performed. All sEVs-treated groups revealed enhanced cellular and odontogenic activities. OD-sEVs enhanced wound healing and mineralization, while LLLT-sEVs showed relatively higher viability, odontogenic gene and protein expression levels. However, no significant differences were detected between both groups. The novel dual preconditioning protocol surpassed either treatment alone representing a promising approach for odontogenic induction of mesenchymal stem cells. The results highlighted the regenerative potential of preconditioned sEVs as a biological, promising pulp capping material that could open new avenues in the field of regenerative endodontic treatment after being tested in-vivo in experimental animals.

title: Dose-dependent effects of photobiomodulation on stem cells from human exfoliated deciduous teeth cultured on polylactic acid films: An in vitro study.
first_affiliation: Postgraduate Program in Dental Sciences, Federal University of Rio Grande Do Norte (UFRN), Natal, Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil.
keywords: stem cells from human exfoliated deciduous teeth

abstract.text: This study investigated the effects of photobiomodulation (PBM) on stem cells from human exfoliated deciduous teeth (SHEDs) cultured on polylactic acid (PLA) films. Cells received a single 660-nm PBM application at nominal radiant exposures of 1 or 4 J/cm2 (L1 and L4); non-irradiated cultures comprised the control group (C). Metabolic activity was assessed by Alamar blue assay at 24, 48, and 72 h, cell cycle distribution by flow cytometry at 72 h, and morphology and surface coverage by scanning electron microscopy at 72 h. L4 showed greater metabolic activity than C at 24, 48, and 72 h, whereas L1 differed from C at 48 and 72 h (p < 0.05); L1 and L4 did not differ significantly. At 72 h, L4 showed a greater G2/M fraction than both C (p < 0.001) and L1 (p < 0.05). Irradiated cells exhibited greater apparent surface coverage while maintaining a fibroblast-like morphology. PBM therefore modulated metabolic activity, cell cycle distribution, and cell-material interactions in SHEDs cultured on PLA films, with the 4 J/cm2 condition showing the most consistent pattern. These results indicate a dose-related effect of PBM at the cell-biomaterial interface and suggest its potential role in tissue engineering approaches.

title: Development and Validation of an Extraoral Condyle Locating Device and Its Effect on Low-Level Laser Therapy in Patients With Skeletal Class II Malocclusion: Protocol for a 2-Phase Randomized Controlled Trial.
first_affiliation: Department of Orthodontics, Datta Meghe Institute of Higher Education and Research, Wardha, Maharashtra, India.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Precise localization of the mandibular condyle is essential for extraoral therapeutic procedures such as low-level laser therapy (LLLT) in patients with skeletal class II malocclusion undergoing myofunctional appliance therapy. Conventional localization methods rely on palpation and visual estimation, which are operator dependent and may compromise reproducibility and treatment outcomes. To address this limitation, a spectacle-mounted extraoral condyle locating device (EOCLD) has been developed to facilitate accurate and consistent condylar targeting.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study aims to develop and validate the EOCLD for precise condylar localization and evaluate its impact on the clinical efficacy of LLLT in patients with skeletal class II malocclusion undergoing myofunctional appliance therapy.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This 2-phase study will be conducted in patients aged 10 to 13 years in a growth phase with skeletal class II malocclusion. In phase 1, the EOCLD will be evaluated for accuracy and reproducibility using standardized lateral cephalometric imaging. In phase 2, a prospective randomized controlled trial will be conducted in which participants undergoing myofunctional appliance therapy will be randomly allocated to either EOCLD-guided LLLT or conventional unguided LLLT. Skeletal and dentoalveolar changes will be assessed using standardized cephalometric analyses, while condylar growth and mandibular changes will be evaluated using pretreatment and posttreatment cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) imaging. Treatment duration, patient-reported comfort, and compliance will also be assessed.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study is self-funded and received approval from the institutional ethics committee on November 28, 2025. Phase 1 data collection took place from May 21 to August 30, 2026, with EOCLD validation performed in 50 participants. As of September 2026, the data are undergoing statistical analysis. Phase 2 is scheduled to commence on December 1, 2026.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This study will establish the clinical validity of the EOCLD and determine whether guided LLLT enhances treatment efficiency and skeletal outcomes in skeletal class II therapy.

abstract.label: TRIAL REGISTRATION
abstract.text: Clinical Trials Registry-India CTRI/2026/02/102982; https://tinyurl.com/4t3bwrnz.

title: Extreme Diagnostic and Therapeutic Heterogeneity Limits Treatment Conclusions in Iliotibial Band Syndrome: A Systematic Review with Level-of-Evidence Stratification.
first_affiliation: Department of Biomedical Sciences, Humanitas University, Pieve Emanuele, Milan, Italy.

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Iliotibial band syndrome (ITBS) is a leading cause of lateral knee pain in runners and endurance athletes, yet clinical decision-making remains inconsistent and largely unsupported by high-quality comparative evidence. No comprehensive synthesis has previously integrated all available treatment modalities using a standardized evidence framework, and the evidence base for individual injection-based therapies continues to evolve rapidly.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To evaluate all available treatment strategies for ITBS and stratify their efficacy according to the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (CEBM) levels of evidence.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261374567) on 20 April 2026. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 29 April 2026. Screening, data extraction, and the subsequent review processes were completed by 21 May 2026. An updated search subsequently identified one further eligible trial, published after the original cut-off.
